s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic and laboratory evidence of myocardial injury, complicated by hypotension
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain with increasing intensity
ST-segment elevation in multiple leads on ECG
Elevation of high-sensitive troponin T level
Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery on emergency angiography
key_facts: The patient is an older woman
The patient has a history of diabetes
The patient has a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain
The intensity of pain increased over time
Initial vital signs showed a normal heart rate and blood pressure
Blood pressure later fell to 60/40 mm Hg
ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
ECG showed subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9
ECG showed downward-sloping ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4
High-sensitive troponin T level was elevated at 0.309 ng/mL
Emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
Computer tomography angiography revealed contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion

shortlist.label: myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: ECG showed ST-segment elevation and elevated high-sensitive troponin T level, consistent with myocardial infarction

shortlist.label: acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery, consistent with acute myocardial infarction

shortlist.label: coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain and had a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, increasing the likelihood of coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Computer tomography angiography revealed pericardial effusion, which can be associated with pericarditis

shortlist.label: takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain and had a significant increase in pain intensity over time, which can be consistent with takotsubo cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sudden-onset chest pain, ECG findings of ST-segment elevation in multiple leads, elevated high-sensitive troponin T level, and emergency angiography showing thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery are all consistent with acute myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: myocardial infarction
rejected.why: While myocardial infarction is a correct diagnosis, acute myocardial infarction is more specific and better explains the patient's acute presentation.

rejected.label: coronary artery disease
rejected.why: Coronary artery disease is a broader term that encompasses acute myocardial infarction, but it does not specifically explain the patient's acute symptoms and ECG findings.

rejected.label: pericarditis
rejected.why: Pericarditis typically presents with chest pain that improves with sitting up and worsens with lying down, and ECG findings of widespread ST-segment elevation without reciprocal changes, which is not consistent with this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy typically presents with transient left ventricular dysfunction in the absence of significant coronary artery disease, which is not consistent with the patient's emergency angiography findings of thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery.
